headline_hook: Washington Decides Who Gets GPT-5.6 While Anthropic Unshackles the API
preview_topics: GPT-5.6 Sol and its government gatekeepers
what 2,000 hackers learned attacking an AI assistant

pick_of_the_day.thesis: State-gated access to commercial models isn't a one-off policy quirk — it's the birth of a tiered distribution system that will split the AI market by geography and clearance level, forcing every builder to plan for a world where frontier capabilities have border controls.

model_literacy.relevance: With GPT-5.6 and Mythos both subject to government vetting, today's news makes concrete the idea that models cross invisible lines where their capabilities trigger regulatory intervention — understanding where those thresholds sit determines whether your product can access frontier models at all.

items.title: OpenAI previews GPT-5.6 'Sol' — the next frontier benchmark
items.angle: The first official look at Sol: what capabilities OpenAI is telegraphing, and why the preview-before-release cadence itself signals a shift in how frontier models get rolled out.
items.key_fact: GPT-5.6 is codenamed Sol and comes with government-level access vetting — a first for OpenAI

items.title: Anthropic unifies Claude API rate limits — Sonnet and Haiku match Opus
items.angle: Five tiers collapse to three, every model gets the same ceiling, and most orgs auto-upgrade. The rate limit wall that forced production workarounds is gone.
items.key_fact: Tiers consolidate from five to three (Start, Build, Scale); Sonnet and Haiku now match Opus limits at every tier

items.title: DeepReinforce drops Ornith-1.0 — a 9B/35B/397B model family hits HuggingFace
items.angle: A full model family spanning edge to datacenter, with the 35B landing in the sweet spot for local deployment and GGUF already available for the 9B.
items.key_fact: Three sizes (9B, 35B, 397B) all trending on HuggingFace simultaneously; 9B has GGUF quantizations ready

items.title: Liquid AI ships LFM2.5 at 230M params — ultra-small models for edge inference
items.angle: At 230M parameters, LFM2.5 targets the embedded and on-device slot that transformers struggle to fill. 8K+ downloads in hours.
items.key_fact: 230M parameters; 8,300+ downloads already; designed for edge and embedded deployment

items.title: The U.S. government will decide who gets GPT-5.6 — a first for commercial AI
items.angle: State-level access control on a commercial model is unprecedented. This isn't export policy — it's the government inserting itself into the API onboarding flow.
items.key_fact: First major commercial AI model where the U.S. government vets individual users before granting access

items.title: Anthropic's Mythos cleared for 'trusted partners' by U.S. government
items.angle: A second frontier model under government distribution control in the same week. The pattern is now undeniable: tiered access is the new normal for frontier AI.
items.key_fact: Limited release to vetted domestic partners only — mirrors the GPT-5.6 access structure

items.title: OpenAI's internal AI usage exploded 56x in Research since November 2025
items.angle: The company building the models is also the most aggressive user. 56x growth in Research output tokens means AI-generated text is becoming the default medium for internal work.
items.key_fact: Median output tokens grew 56x in Research, 32x in Customer Support, 27x in Engineering, 13x in Legal

items.title: The real gap between open-weights and closed models in 2026
items.angle: A data-driven look at where open models actually compete and where they don't — especially relevant now that government controls are creating artificial scarcity at the frontier.
items.key_fact: Analysis published alongside GLM-5.2's gains and the new government access tiers for GPT-5.6 and Mythos

items.title: What 2,000 people learned trying to hack Simon Willison's AI assistant
items.angle: The largest public red-team dataset for a consumer AI product. Real attack patterns, real defenses, and the failure modes that surprised even the builder.
items.key_fact: 2,000 participants; detailed breakdown of successful and failed prompt injection patterns

items.title: CVE-2026-LGTM post-mortem: when AI security goes wrong in production
items.angle: A detailed incident analysis that turns abstract AI security risks into concrete production lessons — the kind of post-mortem that should be required reading before shipping AI-facing features.
items.key_fact: Full incident timeline and root-cause analysis from Simon Willison

items.title: A modern GPU programming course built for ML systems in 2026
items.angle: MLC.ai's course covers the kernel and memory patterns that actually matter for inference optimization — not GPU programming in general, but the specific subset ML engineers need.
items.key_fact: Free, comprehensive course covering kernels and memory patterns for inference and training

items.title: WorkWeave ships an open-source model router for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor
items.angle: Automatic model selection per task without changing your workflow — 133 HN upvotes suggest developers want routing as infrastructure, not configuration.
items.key_fact: Open-source; plugs into Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor; 133 HN upvotes in hours

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.195 fixes hook matching and adds fullscreen mode controls
items.angle: The hook matcher fix is the real story — hyphenated identifiers like code-reviewer and mcp__brave-search were substring-matching, causing false triggers.
items.key_fact: Fixes hook matchers that substring-matched hyphenated identifiers; adds CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS env var

items.title: Lemma Platform: an open-source workspace where humans and agents collaborate
items.angle: Positions itself as the team coordination layer on top of individual coding agents — the missing piece between 'agent writes code' and 'team ships product.'
items.key_fact: Open-source; 110 GitHub stars; trending on GitHub in AI/Python

items.title: GITVERSE reverse-engineers any repo into an AI-ready build prompt
items.angle: Converts a codebase into an architecture breakdown with a reconstruction prompt — useful for onboarding coding agents to unfamiliar repos without manual context dumps.
items.key_fact: 98 GitHub stars; TypeScript; generates portable project blueprints from any repo

quick_links.title: Vercel AI SDK adds first-class audio generation
quick_links.angle: generateAudio joins text and image as a unified SDK call
quick_links.key_fact: AI SDK v6.0.213; audio is now a first-class generation mode

quick_links.title: langchain-anthropic fixes streaming truncation bug
quick_links.angle: First tokens of streamed responses were silently dropped on content_block_start
quick_links.key_fact: v1.4.8; fixes dropped initial text in streaming responses

quick_links.title: llama.cpp optimizes multi-GPU sync for faster inference
quick_links.angle: Async CPU-to-CUDA copy with relaxed sync reduces multi-GPU idle time
quick_links.key_fact: Build b9820; less synchronization overhead for split compute

quick_links.title: CrewAI patches SSRF redirect bypass in agent scraping
quick_links.angle: Security fix for agents that fetch external URLs
quick_links.key_fact: v1.15.1a1; SSRF redirect bypass patched in scraping fetches

quick_links.title: IEEE Spectrum: AI is forcing epistemological questions in mathematics
quick_links.angle: From proof verification to conjecture generation — what counts as understanding?
quick_links.key_fact: IEEE Spectrum feature on AI reshaping mathematical research methods
